text: By supporting our high-performing firms in Singapore, we hope to uplift the capacity and capabilities of our entire industry ecosystem, including our local SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Mark Lee and Mr Edward Chia asked how the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) intends to support the financing needs of businesses as they expand globally.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This caters to enterprises with longer and more complex growth trajectories that will require more time to fully realise their potential.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Unlike traditional debt, private credit has the flexibility to meet the specific needs of companies looking to scale up quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And unlike equity, private credit allows companies and founders to retain business ownership and control.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The PCGF is targeted at local enterprises with strong growth potential to become leaders in their respective industry domain.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some of them will require tailored financing solutions to support their unique growth strategy, such as international merger and acquisitions (M&As) or large overseas capital investments.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These solutions may not be readily available in Asia, through the traditional financing today.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Beyond the $1 billion seeded by the Government, we hope to catalyse more commercial funding as more fund managers and investors gain familiarity and confidence in this space.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I spoke earlier about the importance of our pro-enterprise environment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At last year's National Day Rally, the Prime Minister also spoke about the need for us to ensure a business-friendly environment and to keep regulatory burden to a minimum.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We had set up the Inter-Ministerial Committee for Pro-Enterprise Rules Review last year that I chair to look into our rules and streamline our regulations, to enable our businesses to move fast to seize the opportunities that come our way.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Since then, my fellow Ministers and I have engaged more than 140 business leaders across 14 sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Business leaders have cited approval timelines, frequency of licence renewals and duplicative processes as key areas for improvement.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While we will tackle specific feedback from the industry, and Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling will elaborate later, the Government will set three Statements of Commitment to guide our whole-of-Government efforts to increase regulatory agility and reduce compliance burden for our businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, all relevant agencies will publish service standards for the processing of business regulatory applications to provide greater clarity for companies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will endeavour to streamline service standards to 30 working days or less, where feasible.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second, we will increase the validity period of regular business licences to a minimum of three years where possible and aim towards five years.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will provide greater certainty for businesses, especially for those undertaking longer-term growth plans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Third, the Government will continue to streamline regulatory processes to facilitate concurrent rather than sequential approvals where possible.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also streamline information requests across agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have made good progress in the Built Environment sector, by developing CORENET X as a one-stop digital platform for building works approvals across agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We should learn from this experience and apply the same approach in other domains.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Lastly, we are investing more in our people.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ultimately, we pursue economic growth so that future generations of Singaporeans can continue to build better lives for themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: So, this growth must translate into real opportunities for Singaporeans to advance their careers and develop their potential to the fullest.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Lifelong learning is critical for workers to upgrade themselves and take up higher wage roles.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will also help businesses develop and retain their local manufacturing talent pipeline and enhance business continuity.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also strengthen initiatives to groom more Singaporean Global Leaders.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One of 60 fellows from the pioneer batch is Ms Camy Loh.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Camy joined Royal Vopak, a leading independent tank storage company, as a sales manager in Singapore in 2014.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Today, Camy is now the Deputy Managing Director of Royal Vopak's Thai Tank Terminal, co-leading a team of over 120 employees at one of the largest maritime logistics terminals near Bangkok.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It was a big step for her professionally as well as personally.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Through the SGLN, Camy gained skills and knowledge to allow her to thrive in this role in Bangkok.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) will elaborate further on this.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These education and training initiatives take time to bear fruit, and I encourage companies to start early and proactively plan to nurture Singaporean talent and benefit from a strong pipeline of talent and leadership.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In fact, I think I should say that we are already in uncharted waters.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will face economic uncertainties and disruptions in the months and years to come.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There will be challenges, but there will also be opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is how we will earn our living and standing in an increasingly uncertain and unfavourable external environment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: By doing so, we will keep our economy going, keep our economy strong, vibrant and resilient, and create better jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans and a better future for Singapore for the next 60 years and more.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our population is ageing rapidly amidst intensifying competition for talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We face fiercer rivalry for investments as we navigate land and carbon constraints.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To address these challenges, we will expand our resource potential through four strategies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Third, sustaining investments in research and innovation and last, but not least, enhancing our land productivity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I will first update on our decarbonisation efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean said, Singapore is a climate realist.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The timeline for climate action is set by nature, not geopolitical developments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Moreover, our decarbonisation initiatives are an important factor in companies' investment decisions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We owe it to our children and our grandchildren to stay the course.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Cross-border electricity trading is crucial to achieving our climate goals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are working towards progressing the first batch of electricity import projects with Conditional Licences, to reach Final Investment Decisions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These projects are win-win collaborations that lay the groundwork for our shared aspiration of an ASEAN Power Grid within the region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Concurrently, we will maximise our domestic solar potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This puts us on track to achieving our 2030 target of at least two GWp.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Scaling beyond the two GWp is challenging, but we will continue to encourage home owners and building owners to install solar panels and push the boundaries of domestic deployment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For example, the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) has worked with industry stakeholders, including through the Alliance for Action (AfA) on Business Competitiveness, to simplify regulatory processes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Electricity imports and solar energy alone are insufficient to get us to net-zero.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We need to explore every possible decarbonisation pathway.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Nuclear energy, especially advanced nuclear reactors, is an option that we are seriously studying for potential deployment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Now, let me address Mr Sharael Taha and Ms Jessica Tan's questions clearly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have not yet made a decision on deployment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is, therefore, premature to speak on potential sites, costs and specific plans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But our current priority is to accelerate capability building on nuclear safety and advanced nuclear technologies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are training more nuclear scientists, such as via postgraduate scholarships in nuclear science and engineering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are also stepping up on international partnerships.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Last year, we signed a substantive civil nuclear agreement with the United States.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This complements our ongoing cooperation with partners, such as the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), France's Institute for Radiological Protection and Nuclear Safety and the Emirates Nuclear Energy Company.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about our plans for hydrogen.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Hydrogen, indeed, has the potential to be a low-carbon fuel for the future, although high adoption costs and technical challenges remain today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In the near-term, our focus is similarly on capability building.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: By the end of this year, the Energy Market Authority (EMA) and Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) aim to identify a lead developer for a pilot project to use ammonia for power generation and maritime bunkering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are also exploring complementary solutions to decarbonise the hard-to-abate sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies are advancing quickly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will engage emitters and potential service providers to develop the CCS value chain and partner countries with suitable geological storage sites.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have made progress by signing a Letter of Intent with Indonesia in 2024 and a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Malaysia in 2025.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Edward Chia and Ms Tin Pei Ling asked for an update on our carbon markets initiatives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean mentioned, Singapore just signed an Implementation Agreement with Bhutan, in addition to our agreements with Ghana and Papua New Guinea.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These Agreements establish the framework for the transfer of Article 6 carbon credits, which is aligned with our environmental integrity criteria.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MTI will also be launching a Request for Proposals to procure Article 6-compliant carbon credits later this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat pointed out, natural gas will continue to play a crucial role in our energy mix.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And that is why we will set up the central gas procurement entity for the power sector this year and complete the development of our second liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal by this decade.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These will secure our natural gas needs for the foreseeable future.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will calibrate our speed of adoption for energy technologies and solutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: International and local players, like IHI Corporation from Japan and CRecTech, a local company, have already expressed interest to use LCT3.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For commercially-mature solutions, we will accelerate their deployment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As Mr Saktiandi Supaat highlighted, this includes making major infrastructural investments for a low-carbon future.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have not disbursed monies from the fund, as it is still early days in our infrastructural developmental journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, we anticipate significant drawdowns once key technological and commercial thresholds are crossed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To better inform our decisions as we decarbonise, A*STAR is developing an integrated model to simulate the interdependencies of the possible net-zero mitigation measures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Members have voiced concerns about the potential impact of decarbonisation on energy costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our aim is to strike the right balance between decarbonisation towards net zero, ensuring at the same time our energy security and maintaining cost-competitiveness.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For households, we will continue to provide support through measures, such as U-save rebates.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For businesses, we will co-fund investments in energy efficiency through initiatives like the Energy Efficiency Grant.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Furthermore, we will fully rechannel carbon tax revenue collected towards decarbonisation efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We do not expect, therefore, to derive additional net revenue from the carbon tax in this decade.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As we decarbonise, we will continue to upgrade the skillsets of our workforce.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is particularly crucial for workers in energy-intensive sectors, such as the petrochemicals industry, who will be more impacted by the green transition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Many already possess core skillsets that allow them to take on new job opportunities in adjacent growth segments, like specialty chemicals, or those in the sustainability space.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also support workers via CET efforts, as well as Career Conversion Programmes (CCPs).

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Beyond the green transition, CET will remain a key enabler to deepen Singaporeans' skills in response to digitalisation and AI.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will continue to work with companies and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to support workers in upskilling and attaining better wage outcomes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One prime example is EDB's collaboration with industry and the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) on an Electrical and Electronics Engineering degree for in-employment diploma holders in manufacturing roles.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This CET degree follows best practices in adult education by recognising prior learning and work experiences and allowing qualifications to be stacked towards a degree.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Learners can also access recorded lessons and online consultations, so that it is easier for them to juggle work and study.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: CCPs can also support the reskilling and the redeployment of employees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Mark Lee would be pleased to know that Workforce Singapore's (WSG's) CCPs already support these redeployments of existing employees post-merger.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Now, even as we develop Singaporeans, we must continue to attract global talent that can complement our local workforce.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have concluded agreements with both Indonesia and Vietnam to facilitate the exchange of technology and innovation talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Tech:X pilot with Indonesia was launched in July last year, while the parameters of the Innovation Talent Exchange programme with Vietnam were launched in September 2024.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, Indonesia in July 2024 and Vietnam in September 2024.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Nearly 50 companies and 50 Singaporeans have expressed interest across both programmes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our young leaders will have greater exposure to regional economies and companies will find it easier to access mobile talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Collectively, this two-pronged strategy of supporting Singaporeans and attracting global talent will keep our workforce globally competitive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I will elaborate on how our efforts have supported good employment outcomes for Singaporeans later at MOM's Committee of Supply (COS) debate this evening.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har asked how we will drive research translation and support the development of our semi-conductors and biotech sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Last week, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat announced upcoming initiatives, such as the RIE Flagship to advance semi-conductor R&D and the RIE Grand Challenge, focusing on healthy and successful longevity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These complement the existing R&D translation platforms available.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One such platform is A*STAR's MedTech Catapult, which provides infrastructure, expertise and connections to local contract manufacturers looking to further develop frontier medical devices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I attended the launch event last month and was happy to know that more than 10 companies have applied to this initiative.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Besides this, the NSTIC (R&D Fab) for advanced packaging in semi-conductors, which Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong shared earlier, is another R&D translation platform that A*STAR will be rolling out.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Such investments enable more firms to produce cutting-edge technologies, create good jobs and maintain Singapore's competitiveness.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To address Ms Foo Mee Har's question on securing the talent pipeline for our R&D facilities, we are bringing in top talent who contribute to the ecosystem.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: During COS 2023, I shared about Prof Watson, an Overseas Networks and Expertise Pass (ONE PASS) holder, who took on the Executive Director role at A*STAR Skin Research Labs and the Skin Research Institute of Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Prof Watson has since strengthened A*STAR's global standing, by partnering the National Skin Centre and Sanofi to trial a first-of-its-kind acne vaccine and deepen understanding of key biological markers that impact the severity of the condition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These are signs that our efforts are bearing fruit and we will invest further.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First, A*STAR will be located closer to key partners, like the National University Health System's clinical community and venture builders, making it a new attraction point for both industry players and talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second, A*STAR will redesign its laboratories and workspaces to promote interdisciplinary collaboration across the different research institutes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It will do so by providing more centrally-managed collaboration spaces that allow for better integration of expertise across teams.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: A*STAR will also introduce new biopharma manufacturing programmes with its partners – the Singapore Cell Therapy Advanced Manufacturing Programme 2.0 (STAMP 2.0) and the Process Accelerator for Cell Therapy Manufacturing (PACTMAN).

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Cell therapies, such as chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy, have transformed treatment for certain blood cancers and they have demonstrated promise for autoimmune diseases, but they remain complex and expensive to manufacture.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Since 2019, STAMP has partnered biotech companies to improve the quality testing of cell therapy assets, conduct CAR-T therapy trials in Singapore and enable licensing and spinoffs of new technologies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: STAMP 2.0 will build on this to develop lower-cost manufacturing technologies that can produce higher quality products.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For example, it aims to reduce the time taken for cell extraction, modification and infusion into patients, what we call the vein-to-vein time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Meanwhile, PACTMAN will develop scalable processes to accelerate the translation of cell therapies, including those developed through STAMP, from laboratory to clinic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Taken together, these efforts will deepen our R&D capabilities and drive innovation-led growth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Companies receiving the LIA approval during the next five years will continue to enjoy tax allowance on the full qualifying costs over 15 years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: From 2026, we will make it easier for companies to qualify for LIA so that they can optimise space and they can integrate operations with related businesses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Building users and LIA recipients can be considered related if they own more than 50% shareholding of each other.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is down from the current threshold of at least 75%.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: JTC will also introduce four initiatives to provide greater flexibility for companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These initiatives support the recommendations from the AfA on Business Competitiveness and the work under the Inter-Ministerial Committee for Pro-Enterprise Rules Review.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First, companies with new leases on greenfield industrial land will be offered additional three years of lease tenure to cover the development and building period.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will allow companies to enjoy the full duration of the lease with their completed development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second, high-performing companies will have more flexibility to extend their leases in shorter periods for incremental business investments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Third, JTC will bring forward the lease renewal application period from the current six years to ten years before lease expiry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will now recognise auditable investments in innovation, R&D, digital transformation and intellectual property (IP) creation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: (In Mandarin):   There is an old saying, "Wealth does not last beyond three generations." However, through the hard work of successive generations, Singapore has successfully entered its fourth generation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We, as the current generation, should uphold the same spirit and be accountable to future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The measures that I have announced today will lay the foundations for the future of Singapore's economy. : Chairman, as we conclude, let us reflect on the enduring Singapore spirit.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For 60 years, we have thrived not despite our challenges but because of them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have always been tight on resources, but we are never short on resourcefulness.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our resource constraints have compelled us to be innovative and brought us to where we are today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong shared that the next chapter of our economic journey will bring new challenges and opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have what it takes to stay anchored amid the waves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Over the years, our enterprises have acquired the skills to adapt, innovate and change to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Together, we can transform to achieve growth and stay ahead of the game.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government is strongly committed to supporting our enterprises every step of the way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To enable their business transformation and growth, we will: one, support the overseas expansion of our enterprises; two, empower our enterprises to transform and benefit from artificial intelligence; and three, enhance Singapore's pro-enterprise business environment and reduce red tape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will also boost our heartlands and support our heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, Singapore's economic success is built on our ability to connect with the world, as Mr Mark Lee has noted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For Singapore enterprises to grow, they must expand beyond our hinterland to overseas markets for fresh revenue streams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to reassure Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Edward Chia, Mr Mark Lee and Mr Keith Chua that Enterprise Singapore is committed to providing comprehensive and holistic support for Singapore enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Companies that undertook internationalisation projects saw a projected increase in annual revenue of $8.8 million per company compared to $7.7 million in 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I am glad to announce that moving forward, we will further enhance our support in this area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have considered feedback from the business community, including the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) and PricewaterhouseCoopers, and would like to meet this need for financing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Enterprises with expansion plans can continue to benefit from a 200% tax deduction on eligible expenses for overseas market expansion and investment development activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They are restarting their expansion plans and need more time to execute their global market outreach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides our grant, tax and financing schemes, Enterprise Singapore and its partners operate a wide network of Overseas Centres where Singapore SMEs can receive support to enter regional markets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides helping enterprises grow their overseas markets, I want to reassure Mr Mark Lee that the Government will enhance support for enterprises pursuing inorganic growth via M&A.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will expand the scope of the Enterprise Financing Scheme – Mergers and Acquisitions (EFS-M&A) to also cover targeted asset acquisitions, such as intellectual properties and contracts, without a corresponding equity purchase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will help unlock loan financing for enterprises to acquire specific and complementary assets of a target business that can enhance their growth prospects without having to buy out the target business and, therefore, take on its liabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The pilot will last five years, from 1 April this year until 31 March 2030.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, in addition to providing access to financing, we will continue to support enterprises in adopting new technologies, such as AI, because AI can spur enterprise and workforce transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It enables the firm to automate manual business processes and augment workers' skills, raising productivity, driving innovation and further growing business revenue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) will share the broad progress of our National AI Strategy (NAIS) 2.0 while I will focus on MTI's key industry development efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, we will support more enterprises in setting up AI centres of excellence to accelerate the development and deployment of AI solutions across our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We recognise that enterprises need access to compute infrastructure, software and consultancy services to grow their AI R&D and productisation capabilities And so, as the Prime Minister announced and mentioned in his Budget Statement, we are introducing the new Enterprise Compute Initiative (ECI) for Singapore-based enterprises with the ambition to anchor AI mandates and grow AI teams here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Enterprises which are digitally mature, have a compelling AI use case as well as an implementation roadmap can tap on the ECI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Mark Lee will be pleased to know that under ECI, participants will have access to cloud compute credits and training programmes from cloud service providers, such as Google, Microsoft and Amazon Web Services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government will also provide a grant for ECI participants to access consultancy services offered by system integrators to help them develop and scale their AI solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Jessica Tan will be pleased to know that Enterprise Singapore, in partnership with the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), has helped close to 3,000 SMEs adopt AI solutions through the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will continue to enhance our existing digitalisation initiatives, such as the SMEs Go Digital Programme, to accelerate AI adoption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MDDI will elaborate more on this during their COS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides powering up enterprises to use AI, we will help workers to upskill and harness AI to advance their careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa will be glad to know that we are indeed deepening our partnerships with the industry and the IHL partners to continue delivering industry-relevant curricula and providing student internships.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MOM will share more details on how we will enhance support for businesses as they redesign jobs and upskill workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, Singapore is continuing to innovate and stay agile with AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The constant energy to do better is part of our Singapore DNA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Gan spoke about our business-friendly environment, a fundamental quality that has enabled Singapore to stay attractive, to stay competitive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are not resting on our laurels and we are committed to doing more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government has stepped up our engagements with the industry and sought views on how Singapore can strengthen our competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To this end, I co-chaired the AfA on Business Competitiveness with SBF Council Vice Chairman Mr Mark Lee from February to November last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Neil Parekh will also know and, in fact, he shared that the AfA engaged the businesses, and trade associations and chambers (TACs) extensively last year and released 27 recommendations on manpower, land and regulatory issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our Government agencies have considered the AfA's recommendations seriously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Earlier on, you heard from Second Minister Dr Tan See Leng, JTC will implement the AfA's recommendation on lease tenure and renewals for industrial land.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In April 2024, the Government formed the Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) for Pro-Enterprise Rules Review to review our regulatory regime for the next bound.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First is the SME Pro-Enterprise Office (SME PEO).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Working with the Pro-Enterprise Panel and respective regulatory agencies, SME PEO will be the Government's key coordination unit to aggregate business feedback and to improve regulations at the systems level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We seek continued strong support from our key partners, including the SBF and all TACs, to be our ears on the ground as well as champions for SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Let us work closely with SME PEO to reduce red tape and to streamline processes to support our SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, there are 10 SME Centres across Singapore, helmed by TACs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Business Advisors at these Centres will be armed with new toolkits to provide enhanced one-to-one business advisory services, workshops as well as group-based upgrading projects where multiple businesses facing similar pain points can adopt a common solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This complements the work of the SME PEO so that our businesses can receive advisory support for their growth needs, including regulatory issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will continue to partner closely with our TACs to enhance SME Centres' offerings and to extend our reach to more businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Third, we will continue investing in and improving our digital platforms, such as the GoBusiness portal and the Enterprise Singapore's Business Grants Portal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will not only streamline licensing and regulatory transactions, but we will also improve, in terms of the grant applications, to better serve businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Enterprise Singapore continues to enhance its grant processing efficiency through automation and centralised processing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, the processing time for PSG applications has been shortened by 80%, from the previous almost three months to the current two weeks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These enhancements to our grant application and approval processes for local enterprises will not stop.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will continue to look at how we can improve and shorten the processing time by leveraging automation and centralised processing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Taken together, the three pillars – the SME PEO, SME Centres and digitalisation – will continue to drive our efforts in supporting business transformation and growth for our SMEs and our enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, while easing regulatory burdens for businesses, the Government is also mindful that for markets to function properly, consumers' trust in merchants and markets must be upheld.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: On Mr Dennis Tan's suggestion, while right-to-repair has its benefits to the environment and to consumers, there are also potential downsides, such as data security concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure him that we will monitor and assess the need for such legislation in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I also want to assure Ms Sylvia Lim that there is a whole-of-Government approach today to deal with scams which are criminal in nature, led by MHA and coordinated by the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Scams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MTI and the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) regularly review our consumer protection regime to ensure that consumers' interests are protected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act (or CPFTA) provides general remedies for consumers who encounter unfair trade practices when transacting with businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, sector regulators have established more specific standards relevant to the sectors they oversee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: An effective consumer protection regime also requires the strong support of our key partners and businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MTI works closely with the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) to raise consumer awareness and champion their needs and rights.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Mr Melvin Yong that more can be done, especially in the e-commerce space, where unfair practices can take on new and less-obvious forms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government welcomes and encourages businesses to take the lead in industry-led initiatives, to ensure a fair and safe marketplace for our consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have commenced consulting with the industry and will announce more details on our upcoming initiatives in the coming weeks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last but not least, let me speak on something closer to home – heartland shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many of us have very close ties to the heartlands, where we live, work and share good memories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They form part of our collective identity as Singaporeans, and our heartland shops are really part and parcel of our daily lives and social fabric.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I reassure Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Keith Chua that we are sparing no efforts to rejuvenate our heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have made progress in the past few years and we will strive to do more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In fact, earlier in October 2020, we laid the foundation for transformation with the Heartlands Go Digital Programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In 2022 and 2023, we further expanded the Heartlands Go Digital Programme to cover wider areas, such as service excellence, digital marketing and human resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have also helped heartland shops rejuvenate their premises with the Visual Merchandising Programme that was launched in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our heartland shops in Singapore have also benefited from the launch of Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers since the scheme started slightly more than three years ago.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In fact, the new round of CDC Vouchers as well as the SG60 Vouchers this year will again boost the visibility, footfall as well as business for our heartland shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For many of our heartland shops, getting that additional visibility and awareness can really make a vital difference to their business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: That is why, last year, we launched the Heartland Enterprise Placemaking Grant (HEPG) to encourage our heartland merchants to organise innovative placemaking activities involving community engagement, public art installations, workshops, and thematic festivals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many heartland shops have applied successfully for the HEPG.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One such shop is Quan Shui Wet Market, which started in Ang Mo Kio in 1968.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The fresh pork stall owned by Uncle Oh Quan Shui has grown to eight and is now an omni-channel retail operation with a flagship store at Upper Thomson.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Quan Shui participated in the Digital Practitioner Programme (DPP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In fact, under the charge of Uncle Oh's grandson, Neo Jun He, the store has refreshed its brand and pivoted online with a website and marketing a wider range of product range that went beyond just pork.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Within just five months, Quan Shui attracted a growing pool of keen visitors and potential customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And like what Mr Desmond Choo mentioned during his cut yesterday, Quan Shui tapped into the HEPG to improve its product visibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They participated in Easty Breezy, which is a seaside-inspired marketplace last September in Marine Parade, as well as a Chinese New Year Bazaar this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Both events led to higher revenue, footfall and brand loyalty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In fact, with its refreshed brand, expanded online presence and growing product range, Quan Shui's revenue increased by 25% from 2021 to 2024, and the company is projecting a 20% growth year-on-year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, we would like to invite all Members to have a taste of Quan Shui's success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MTI has arranged for bento boxes with Quan Shui's siew mai, har gao as well as the chicken and mushroom dumplings to be served in the Members' Room later during tea break, and we have also made special arrangements for our Muslim Members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have set aside four of their very, very popular halal otah buns in each bento set for each of our Muslim Members when they break fast later.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We hope that Members will enjoy this at the end of the day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These handmade local dim sums are really based on the 60-year-old family recipe from the founder, Uncle Oh.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, companies like Quan Shui, have shown that Government support and schemes helped them to transform and boost their businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to encourage our enterprises to approach any of our 10 SME Centres for assistance and to embark on a journey of transformation and growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Given the success of these initiatives, we will continue strengthening Our Heartlands 2025 Programme with fresh initiatives and energise our heartlands "inside out".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, the project scope for the shopfront makeover can be more customised and more training topics will be added.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They can conduct bite-sized and pre-scoped activities under a recommended standard option or explore holding larger-scale, customised placemaking events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Chairman, fellow Members of Parliament, the global and regional economies are facing unprecedented situations, and all Singapore businesses must actively innovate and transform.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government will support businesses in their transformation and growth in these areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Third, increasing regulatory flexibility to create a business-friendly environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In recent years, we have continuously work to revitalise our heartland economy and promote the development of heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through the new round of CDC Vouchers and the SG60 Vouchers this year, we will continue to help heartland shops and hawkers increase their revenue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our heartland communities are our emotional connection points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For Singaporeans, the familiar heartland shops and hawker stalls play an irreplaceable role in deepening our collective memories and national identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Like the handmade snacks you will enjoy later, our heartland communities have that familiar flavour and human touch.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Therefore, we will further upgrade Our Heartlands 2025 Programme to let communities shine from inside out, injecting vitality throughout our heartland communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These include launching an enhanced Visual Merchandising Scheme, increasing the total qualifying cost five-fold from $12,000 to $60,000, while expanding shop renovation scope and adding training topics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Additionally, we will launch the Vibrant Heartlands Programme for Merchants' Association.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We hope more heartland businesses will make good use of existing schemes for innovation and transformation. : Chairman, the Government is standing together with our Singapore enterprises, with our SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will support and empower our enterprises as they transform and grow be it an SME hoping to expand abroad or an SME embarking on AI or heartland shops and stalls seeking more customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will spare no effort to support them every step of the way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As we forge ahead together, we invite all Singaporeans to join us in energising our heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Let us show them our support during this SG60 year, by patronising our heartland shops and participating in their placemaking activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Let us enjoy and celebrate our vibrant and beloved heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As we do so, we affirm our Singaporean identity with pride and joy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Chairman, the global trading system is coming under severe strain.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are entering uncharted waters, as Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said, marked by heightened geopolitical tensions, rise of economic nationalism and supply chain disruptions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Historically, Singapore has been the gateway to global trade, symbolised by our Singapore River, just outside this chamber.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It has shaped our nation's identity – open, connected and adaptable to shifting global tides.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our rivers thrive when its waters flow freely, so too must we keep our economic pathways flowing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We can do that by connecting Singapore to the world and connecting the world to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We must always connect the world to Singapore, and flow people, businesses and trade through our shores.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They were drawn by the new and refreshed experiences we curated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our live entertainment scene sparkled last year, as we hosted international A-listers like Taylor Swift, Coldplay and Jay Chou.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This year, we already have a few top acts, including Seventeen in January and G.E.M. over the weekend.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have a flow of exciting performances lined up this year as well, including our very own Stefanie Sun, KISS OF LIFE, BTS' j-hope's first solo concert and BABYMONSTER.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also saw strong flow on our Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) front.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Events like Singapore Airshow, Asia Pacific Maritime, and Food & Hotel Asia – Food & Beverage, all drew record numbers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also partnered global world-class intellectual properties (IPs) to curate innovative experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, ArtScience Museum hosted The World of Studio Ghibli; and at Resorts World Sentosa, Harry Potter: Visions of Magic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also lent support to the Louis Vuitton X Murakami pop-up in Joo Chiat.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Building on these flows, the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) has been working with tourism and lifestyle enterprises on new and fresh opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As Mr Neil Parekh highlighted, our vision for the Tourism 2040 (T2040) roadmap will drive the next chapter of our quality tourism journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: STB will share more about T2040 in the coming months.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also have a good flow of events and attractions lined up this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling, as Parliament's heartland guide, spoke about injecting vibrancy into our heartlands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As Parliament's tourist guide, let me take you through some of the new and rejuvenated offerings around Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, our flow of MICE events remains vibrant, reflecting strong business confidence from organisers and delegates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This year, we will host inaugural events like the Business Aviation Asia Forum and Expo.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Bloomberg's New Economy Forum will also return to Singapore in November for the fifth time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Edward Chia asked how we are working with local arts practitioners to create authentic tourism content.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In January, Singapore Art Week (SAW) 2025 aggregated over 160 art events and featured many local artists.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And for the third time, ART SG returned to Singapore as part of SAW, with 105 galleries from 30 countries and territories around the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To Ms Usha Chandradas' question, signature lifestyle events, including music festivals, increases our appeal to global talent and visitors and this boosts tourism and economic spillovers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They also provide a stage for our local creatives to showcase their talent, like Kin Leonn and Iman Fandi.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: STB will continue working with stakeholders, including our National Arts Council (NAC) to create more opportunities for our local music ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will continue to support these events, through financial and non-financial means, to build a diverse pipeline.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And we welcome compelling music festival proposals that bring strong economic benefits to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For sports fans, we will host the National Basketball Association (NBA) Rising Stars Invitational in June, which will be the first regional youth basketball event in Asia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This comes after we hosted the Singapore Tennis Open and Singapore Smash just last month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our Integrated Resorts will also unveil world-class tourism offerings as part of their ambitious expansion plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: When completed in 2029, Marina Bay Sands' upcoming fourth tower will redefine our iconic skyline.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Over at Resorts World Sentosa, I broke ground for its new waterfront lifestyle development in November 2024, which will feature an exciting new promenade with entertainment, retail and dining experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I also opened Illumination's Minion Land just in time for the March school holidays and, later this year, we will open the Singapore Oceanarium, which will be three times the size of our current SEA Aquarium.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In a few years, we will also open Super Nintendo World at Universal Studios Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Let us now go from the South of Singapore to the North of Singapore in Mandai.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Following the opening of Bird Paradise in 2023, new features in Mandai await all of us this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I launched the public Mandai Boardwalk in January 2025, which offers breathtaking views of Upper Seletar Reservoir and the Central Catchment Nature Reserve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also opening Rainforest Wild ASIA, Singapore's fifth zoological park.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It will be home to 29 iconic animal species.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I visited a few weeks ago for a preview and Minister Grace Fu will officially open it next Wednesday.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Then there is also Mandai Rainforest Resort by Banyan Tree, which opens next month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It blends architecture with nature, offering rooms, including tree houses, nestled in lush greenery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Next year, we look forward to opening the Rainforest Wild Africa.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, this flow of new offerings marks our 60th year of Independence and our tourism sector has come a long way since.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I spend plenty of time with our tourism sector – our workers and our visitors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The amazing tourism offerings we enjoy today is testament to their work over the past 60 years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: That is why I am happy to announce that our attractions are rolling out several deals in celebration of SG60.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are working with the Association of Singapore Attractions (ASA) and our tourism businesses to curate SG60 promotions, including family-friendly bundles and discounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mandai Wildlife Reserve will also offer exclusive deals across its parks from May to August.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will launch these deals on our SG60 website today, so please book and visit our attractions and enjoy these amazing offers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Then let us also go on a cruise!

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is the first-ever Disney Cruise Line ship to homeport in Asia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Many new cruise ships will also be calling in Singapore, including Resorts World Cruises' Star Voyager and the Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection's Luminara.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As cruise lead coordinator for ASEAN, we are working with our neighbours on new sailing itineraries, tapping the fast-growing potential of cruise tourism to attract even more visitors to visit Southeast Asia from Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I discussed this with tourism ministers in Johor just in January 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, I shared how we are connecting the world to Singapore through our robust flow of tourism and attraction offerings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Equally important is to connect Singapore to the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: That is why we are deepening our relationship with our trade partners globally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked how we are strengthening our trade links.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our approach is simple: we are working with our trade partners to harness complementary strengths, improve market access and also to drive mutual growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will unlock more opportunities for businesses, talent and capital to flow efficiently across economies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are doubling down on regional economic integration with our ASEAN partners to create an ecosystem where trade, investments, resources and innovation flow seamlessly, making our region jointly more competitive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong shared about our progress on the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework and the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement (ATIGA) to enhance regional trade networks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Second, we are strengthening bilateral economic ties with key partners, such as US, China, India, Vietnam and Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We commemorated the 20th Anniversary of the US-Singapore Free Trade Agreement last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is a cornerstone agreement which remains one of our most actively used Free Trade Agreements (FTAs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have built upon this foundation in new areas such as the digital economy, AI, supply chain resilience and energy, as Minister Tan See Leng mentioned.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It introduces more liberal and transparent trade rules, so Singapore investors and suppliers can enjoy better market access to China and greater confidence when doing businesses there.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In India, annual bilateral trade has grown over 2.5 times since 2005, from $20 billion to $52.3 billion in 2023.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's official visit in September 2024, Singapore and India agreed to elevate our relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Then in January 2025, President Tharman Shanmugaratnam's State visit to India commemorated 60 years of diplomatic tides.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: During the visit, Singapore companies signed MOUs with the Odisha government, including one signed between Surbana Jurong Group and Odisha on sustainable urban planning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In Vietnam, today, Singapore is among Vietnam's top investors and we are unlocking new investment opportunities for our businesses there.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They will form an integral part of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership upgrade with Vietnam.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Enterprise Singapore and Vietnam's Foreign Investment Agency have also established the Singapore Unit, which is a single point of contact to provide support for Singapore companies investing in Vietnam.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: On Malaysia, Ms Usha Chandradas asked about our arts plans for the JS-SEZ.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will discuss with Malaysia how the arts sector can complement our priority areas in the SEZ.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also ensuring that our businesses can make the full use and the most of the FTAs that we have signed, so that they can gain better access to global markets and benefit from greater efficiency and lower business costs when trading with our FTA partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, we worked with SBF to conduct 11 FTA outreach events last year, attended by over 911 companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I attended some of these together with Mr Mark Lee.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These sessions allow us to provide customised advisory support for Singapore companies to use FTAs for exports and internationalisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked how we are diversifying our trade.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These are all in force across the globe and we are doing more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, we are securing partnerships with regions a little bit further away from us, to help us stay relevant amid global uncertainties and shifting tides.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And that is to enable our businesses to improve supply chain resilience and unlock new market opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As the first FTA between MERCOSUR and a Southeast Asian country, this FTA will pave the way for greater economic cooperation between both our regions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also doing exciting work in the Middle East.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In 2023, we established our first Strategic Partnership with a Middle East country, Saudi Arabia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: At the fourth Saudi Arabia-Singapore Joint Committee meeting last month, we discussed collaboration in connectivity, energy, digital economy and innovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also announced new collaborations in logistics and port automation, and started negotiations to update our existing Bilateral Investment Treaty, which entered into force in 2007.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, we are also strengthening ties with Africa, a vast, young and rapidly growing region with vast potential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In fact, I was just in Rwanda last week to advance discussions on Article 6 carbon credits cooperation, digital and AI, and fintech.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I have also met many Singapore-based companies who are venturing into Africa, including GenZero, an investment firm exploring carbon credit projects in Ghana, Kenya and South Africa.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This year, we will host the Africa Singapore Business Forum, a biennial platform that has connected over 5,000 business leaders from Africa and Asia since 2016.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also continue to broaden our trade partnerships in the digital and green economies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are expanding our networks of Digital Economy Agreements (DEAs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: DEAs help us integrate into the global digital economy and enhance digital trade flows.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Through DEAs, we work with other countries to establish rules and standards around issues like personal data and online consumer protection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They enable our businesses to capitalise on cross-border digital services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have four DEAs in force, and are expanding the network.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last year, we concluded the European Union-Singapore Digital Trade Agreement and are negotiating a DEA with the European Free Trade Association.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As a founding member of the Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (DEPA) alongside Chile and New Zealand, we continue to champion DEPA's expansion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And many countries are keen to join DEPA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last year, the Republic of Korea joined DEPA and Costa Rica's accession is nearly finalised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Accession negotiations with Canada, China and Peru are also ongoing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And other economies, such as the United Arab Emirates (UAE), El Salvador and Ukraine, have also applied to join.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
